title: jank-free-animations
description: Learn about jank-free-animations. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Jank-free animations run smoothly at 60 frames per second without stuttering or dropped frames. Achieving this requires understanding the rendering pipeline, using CSS transforms instead of layout properties, and optimizing JavaScript execution.
Most displays refresh at 60Hz, meaning the browser has 16.67ms (1000ms / 60) to render each frame. Missing this budget causes dropped frames and janky animations.

data.title: Frame Budget Calculation
data.code:
Frame Budget at 60fps:

- Total time per frame: 16.67ms
- Script execution: ~4ms
- Rendering: ~6ms
- Painting: ~4ms
- Composite: ~2.67ms

If any stage exceeds its budget:
- Frame missed = dropped frame
- User perceives jank/stutter
- Poor user experience

Common Causes of Jank:
- Long-running JavaScript (>16ms)
- Layout thrashing (repeated calculations)
- Expensive painting (large gradients, shadows)
- Too many layers to composite
- Garbage collection pauses

Targets:
- Desktop: 60fps (16.67ms per frame)
- High-refresh displays: 120fps (8.33ms per frame)
- Mobile: 60fps (same budget, less CPU power)

data.text: CSS transforms (translate, scale, rotate) don't trigger layout or paint, only composition. Layout properties (top, left, width, height) trigger expensive recalculation and should be avoided for animations.

data.title: Transform vs Layout Animation

data.text: CSS transitions are the most performant way to animate simple state changes. They're hardware-accelerated and run on the compositor thread, avoiding the main thread.

data.title: CSS Transition Examples

data.text: For complex animations that CSS can't handle, use requestAnimationFrame. It schedules your animation callback to run right before the browser's next paint, ensuring optimal timing.

data.title: requestAnimationFrame Animation

data.text: Complex paint operations like large gradients, box shadows, and filters are expensive. Reduce paint complexity by using simpler effects or GPU-accelerated alternatives.

data.title: Optimizing Paint Operations

data.text: Promote elements to their own GPU layers using will-change or transform tricks. This allows the compositor to handle animations independently of the main thread.

data.title: Layer Promotion Techniques

data.text: Use specialized React animation libraries that optimize performance. Framer Motion, React Spring, and AutoAnimate provide performant animations with minimal jank.

data.title: Framer Motion Example
Respect prefers-reduced-motion
data.text: Respect user preferences for reduced motion. Check the prefers-reduced-motion media query and disable or simplify animations for users who prefer reduced motion.

data.title: Reduced Motion Support

terms.definition: Stuttering or dropped frames in animations caused by performance issues that prevent the browser from maintaining 60fps.
Browser API that schedules callbacks to run before the next paint, essential for smooth JavaScript animations.
Using the graphics processing unit to handle rendering tasks like compositing and transforms, improving animation performance.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Target 60fps with 16.67ms frame budget per frame
Use CSS transforms instead of layout properties for animations
CSS transitions are the most performant for simple state changes
Use requestAnimationFrame for complex JavaScript animations
Reduce paint complexity by avoiding expensive effects
Promote elements to GPU layers with will-change for complex animations
Use specialized React animation libraries for optimal performance
data.takeaway: Jank-free animations require understanding the rendering pipeline, using CSS transforms, optimizing paint operations, and respecting user preferences for reduced motion.
